anomaly_def.Name: Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Exhaustion of kernel-enforced per-process or system-wide resources such as file descriptors, shared-memory segments, semaphores, threads, or address space that the database engine depends on but does not directly control.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Saturation or misconfiguration of the network, listener, socket, or connection-management layer that prevents clients or replicas from reliably establishing, maintaining, or using database connections.

When these two root causes manifest together, the database may enter a cascading failure mode: bursts of incoming sessions or large result transfers inflate the number of sockets, file handles, and threads until kernel limits are hit; concurrently, network congestion or listener backlog saturation drives up connection latency and retry storms. Observable symptoms include frequent client timeouts, "too many open files" or "cannot create thread" errors in server logs, spikes of half-open and TIME_WAIT sockets, abrupt termination of background or parallel workers, authentication stalls, and a mix of network wait events and OS-level resource allocation failures. The overlap of network-layer socket buildup with tight kernel limits makes it hard to distinguish whether outages stem from the network or the host itself.

Causally, elevated connection rates or slow data transfer inflate the number and lifespan of sockets and backend processes. Each additional socket consumes a file descriptor and kernel memory; each authenticated session spawns a process or thread. If OS limits on descriptors, processes, or shared memory are low, normal retry behavior from network slowdowns will quickly exhaust those limits, preventing new workers from spawning and amplifying connection queuing. Conversely, once the OS refuses new descriptors or threads, the listener cannot accept or process connections, causing clients to back off and retry, which further floods the network and listener backlog. This positive feedback loop intertwines the two anomalies, escalating from partial degradation to complete service outage and making remediation require simultaneous relief of both kernel resource caps and network/connectivity bottlenecks.

entry.official_description: The Monitor IO thread detected that the source (host:%s port:%u network_namespace:%s) does not belong to the group majority, thence the channel '%s' will try to connect to another source.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with connection establishment, authentication exchange, protocol correctness, network reachability, or client/server communication stability.
entry.solution_guidance: Check endpoint reachability, authentication flow, connection limits, protocol compatibility, transport stability, and client connection lifecycle management.
